record.original_question: Do there exist chaotic symplectic billiards in convex C^1-smooth domains?

evidence.quote: Chaotic symplectic billiards?Problem:do chaotic symplectic billiards in convexC 1- smooth domains exist? A natural candidate is the stadium; there is numerical evidence that this might be the case.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a strictly convex bounded domain whose boundary $\partial\Omega$ is of class $C^1$. The symplectic billiard map $T: \partial\Omega \times \partial\Omega \to \partial\Omega \times \partial\Omega$ is defined as follows: a pair $(x, y)$ with $x \neq y$ in $\partial\Omega$ is mapped to $(y, z)$, where $z \in \partial\Omega$ is the unique point (other than $y$) such that the tangent line to $\partial\Omega$ at $y$ is parallel to the chord $xz$. This map preserves the symplectic (area) form $\omega = dx \wedge dy$ on $\partial\Omega \times \partial\Omega$ away from the diagonal.

Question: Does there exist a strictly convex domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ with $C^1$-smooth boundary such that the associated symplectic billiard map $T$ is chaotic, i.e., is ergodic with positive metric entropy (equivalently, has nonzero Lyapunov exponents almost everywhere) with respect to its invariant measure?

A natural candidate is the stadium domain (the convex hull of two disjoint disks of equal radius), for which numerical evidence suggests chaotic behavior of the symplectic billiard.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in a recent compilation of open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry, where it is stated as an open question with the stadium as a natural candidate supported by numerical evidence. No published proof of existence of chaotic symplectic billiards in convex C^1 domains was located.

status_evidence.title: How smooth can convex chaotic billiard tables be?
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the smoothness threshold for chaotic convex billiard tables.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on the smoothness threshold for chaos in convex billiards, distinct from symplectic billiards.
